name: null_propagation
investigation_steps: Trace the null value backward: which function returned null?
Check the function's return type — is null a valid return?
Find the earliest point where the value could be null-checked
Check if the null comes from external input (API, DB, user) or internal logic
common_misleading_hypotheses: Adding a null check at the crash site (treats symptom, not cause)
The data is always supposed to exist (assumption, not verified)
fix_strategy: Guard at the source (where null is produced), not at the crash site. Add a test that exercises the null path explicitly.
expected_blast_shape: Linear call chain — null propagates through return values until something crashes.

name: race_condition
investigation_steps: Identify shared mutable state — what data is accessed by multiple paths?
Check timing dependencies: does the outcome depend on execution order?
Look for missing locks, missing await, or fire-and-forget async calls
Reproduce under load or with artificial delays to confirm timing sensitivity
common_misleading_hypotheses: Adding a retry/delay (masks the race, doesn't fix it)
It only happens in production (different timing, same bug)
fix_strategy: Eliminate shared mutable state or add proper synchronization. Test with concurrent execution, not just sequential.
expected_blast_shape: Fan-out — multiple code paths converge on shared state.

name: type_coercion
investigation_steps: Find where the type changes — which function receives one type and outputs another?
Check API boundaries: is the value a string from JSON that should be a number?
Look for implicit coercion: string concatenation instead of addition, parseInt without radix
Check if the type is correct at the source and wrong at the consumer
common_misleading_hypotheses: Casting at the crash site (hides the real type boundary)
The API always returns the right type (assumption, not validated)
fix_strategy: Validate and convert at the system boundary (API response, DB query, user input). Add type assertions at the boundary, not at usage sites.
expected_blast_shape: Point source — one boundary produces the wrong type, multiple consumers fail.

name: stale_cache
investigation_steps: Identify all caching layers between source of truth and display
Check cache invalidation logic — when does the cache clear?
Look for derived state that doesn't subscribe to source changes
Check if the issue is a read cache (showing old data) or write cache (not persisting new data)
common_misleading_hypotheses: Clearing all caches (fixes symptom, performance regression)
Adding a manual refresh button (defers the real fix to the user)
fix_strategy: Fix the invalidation logic so the cache clears when the source changes. Test by mutating the source and verifying the consumer sees the update without manual intervention.
expected_blast_shape: Star — one stale source, multiple consumers showing old data.

name: config_drift
investigation_steps: Compare the running config against .env.example or schema
Check if the value exists in one environment but not another
Look for recently changed config keys, renamed variables, or moved files
Verify the config loading order — does a local override shadow a default?
common_misleading_hypotheses: The config works on my machine (environment-specific, not code-specific)
Just add the missing key (doesn't prevent recurrence)
fix_strategy: Add the missing config to .env.example with a comment. Add startup validation that fails fast on missing required config. Test by removing the key and verifying a clear error message.
expected_blast_shape: Isolated — one missing config, one failing component.

name: off_by_one
investigation_steps: Identify the loop or index calculation that's off
Check boundary conditions: empty array, single element, last element
Look for < vs <= or 0-based vs 1-based index confusion
Check if the error is at the start boundary, end boundary, or both
common_misleading_hypotheses: Adding a bounds check at the crash site (hides the calculation error)
It only happens with edge case data (the edge case is the real test)
fix_strategy: Fix the index calculation. Add tests for empty, single-element, and boundary cases. The fix is usually changing < to <= or adjusting by 1.
expected_blast_shape: Point — one calculation, one boundary, one failure.
